paper_title: Insight Agents: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Data Insights
summary:
Insight Agents: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Data Insights - Jincheng Bai, Zhenyu Zhang, Jennifer Zhang, Jason Zhu, 2025

Bai, Zhang, Zhang, and Zhu target production-grade conversational analytics for Amazon sellers, where the system must distinguish in-scope data-insight requests from arbitrary user queries, route valid requests to the correct solver, retrieve structured seller data through APIs, and return either descriptive analytics or higher-level diagnostic business insights under tight latency constraints. The system objective is simultaneous coverage, accuracy, and low response time in a real e-commerce setting rather than open-ended agent autonomy. Their architecture is a hierarchical manager-worker design built on a plan-and-execute RAG workflow: a manager agent performs out-of-domain detection, branch routing, and query augmentation, then dispatches to one of two worker agents, a data presenter for descriptive analytics and an insight generator for diagnostic analysis. To avoid excessive LLM calls, the manager uses a lightweight autoencoder over sentence-transformer embeddings for OOD detection, thresholding reconstruction error by the in-domain mean plus a variance-scaled margin, and a fine-tuned 33M-parameter BERT classifier for routing between presenter and generator branches. Query augmentation explicitly injects temporal context such as the current date and calendar-week boundaries to normalize ambiguous requests like last week.

The worker side is grounded in an API-based data model that decomposes user requests into granular retrieval and aggregation steps, then executes data fetching, transformation, semantic column filtering, and post-processing before generation. The insight generator adds an internal domain-routing stage using a few-shot LLM classifier, then conditions final generation on domain-specific analytical procedures, prompt templates, and expert-authored few-shot exemplars; both branches use in-context learning and chain-of-thought-style prompting for response synthesis. The paper reports deployment to Amazon sellers in the United States and evaluates both component models and end-to-end behavior. On 301 collected questions, the autoencoder OOD detector achieved 0.969 precision, 0.721 recall, and 0.009 s runtime per sample, versus 0.616 precision, 0.971 recall, and 1.665 s for an LLM few-shot baseline. On 178 in-domain routing samples, the fine-tuned BERT router reached 0.83 accuracy at 0.31 s latency, compared with 0.60 accuracy and 2.14 s for an LLM-based classifier. End-to-end human evaluation on 100 benchmark questions found 57 in-scope cases, with mean relevancy 0.977, correctness 0.958, completeness 0.993, question-level accuracy 89.5 percent, and P90 latency 13.56 s.
